messages.text: Me and my wife have three kids. I get paid every two weeks. Do we qualify for SNAP or TennCare?

Happy to help check. I have a few questions to start.

1. How old are you, your wife, and each of the three kids?
2. How much do you get paid before taxes each pay period (every two weeks)? Does your wife have any income too?
I'm 36, my wife is 34. Kids are 10, 6, and 3. I make $1,600 every two weeks before taxes. My wife doesn't work outside the home and has no income.

Thanks, that helps. Two more questions:

1. How much do you pay each month for rent or a mortgage?
2. Do you pay separately for heating or cooling, for other utilities like electric or water, for only a phone, or is everything included in your rent?
Rent is $1,200 a month. We pay for heating and cooling separately, and electric and water on top of that. No phone-only bill or anything else included in the rent.

**Short answer:** You probably can get help from all three. Your family looks *likely* for food assistance (SNAP), for TennCare for the kids, and for WIC for your 3-year-old. This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and you can apply either way.

## Food assistance (SNAP): likely
- **Estimate: about $614 a month.** This is only an estimate. The agency will work out the real amount.
- Your income before taxes counts as about $3,440 a month. That's $1,600 every two weeks, converted to a monthly figure ([7 CFR 273.10](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-273.10)).
- The limits for a family of 5 are $4,191 a month before deductions and $3,224 after. Your income is under both ([USDA's FY 2027 limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola)).
- Your rent and your heating, cooling and utility costs lower the income SNAP counts. That is how the amount drops to about $2,007 ([USDA SNAP eligibility](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility)).
- **Savings:** I didn't ask about these. The federal limit is $3,000 in cash and bank accounts. If you're near that, a caseworker can tell you how it applies.
- **Utility figures:** The utility allowance I used was the latest published one. It was in effect through 9/30/2026, and newer figures weren't available. Your estimate could change a little.
- **Apply:** [OneDHS portal](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or 866-311-4287 ([USDA SNAP directory](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap-directory-entry/tennessee)).

## TennCare / CoverKids: likely for the kids, unlikely for you and your wife
- **Your 10-year-old and 6-year-old are likely.** The limit for kids 6 to 18 is $4,288 a month for a family of 5 ([TennCare guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html)).
- **Your 3-year-old is likely.** The limit for kids 1 to 5 is $4,578 a month.
- **You and your wife look unlikely.** The limit for parents is $3,224 a month, and your income is $3,440. You can still apply.
- **Apply:** [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or 855-259-0701.

## WIC: likely for your 3-year-old
- WIC serves children under 5. Your income is under its limit of $5,964 a month for a family of 5 ([USDA WIC guidelines](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926)).
- WIC also does a short health and nutrition check at the clinic.
- **Apply:** your local health department clinic or 1-800-342-5942 ([Tennessee Dept. of Health](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html)).

## Other help
Dial **211** for free help finding and applying for local programs.

If you pay for child care so you or your wife can work or study, tell me. It could raise the SNAP estimate. When you apply, report your income and household accurately. That protects you from having to pay benefits back.
